_comment: Unit tests for the Interaction Contract (INTERACTION_DRAFT.md).
Each case is a snippet of assistant output plus the rule ids a correct
reviewer must flag, and ids it must NOT flag. The must_not list is what
keeps a grader honest: a reviewer that flags everything scores well on
must_flag alone and is useless. Positive controls carry an empty
Graded by a cheap delegate; see grader-prompt.md.

cases.text: I claimed the discriminator is 'a reserved slot'.
cases.why: Unnamed referent (discriminator between what and what), a two-word noun phrase carrying three concepts, pure mechanism with no user anchor, and neither the failure case nor the proposed solution.

cases.text: The build now uses two profiles and the cache was moved under the target directory and clippy no longer re-runs on unchanged crates and the harness reads FEATURES from the Makefile so the gate and the tests agree and this also fixed the incremental rebuild that was evicting artifacts.
cases.why: Six distinct elements in one unsegmented paragraph. Length is NOT the defect and must not be flagged as one.

cases.text: Shortened my explanation to save your time: the daemon rows changed.
cases.why: Answered 'too long' by cutting words rather than adding segmentation, and states a change with no Before/After or solution.

cases.text:
Model settings are appropriate @
Model=Opus Effort=4 Thinking=off
cases.why: Printed, so M1 and M2 are satisfied. Names no next step, so it is a stamp rather than an evaluation.

cases.text: I implemented the first nine items. Before I start the tenth: did you mean the blue threshold applies to every field, or only the ones with streamed bounds?
cases.why: The question was answerable from the original message and should have been asked at receipt. It did not block, so K4 is satisfied.

cases.text:
| 4 | Pending insights | Deferred to last |
| 5 | Crash report table | Not started |
cases.why: Rows neither live nor changed since the previous turn; the table exists and leads, so E1 and E9 hold.

cases.text: | 2 | Tier A gate | running in background |
cases.why: An in-flight row with no elapsed-vs-expected and nothing named that will confirm it finished. It IS live, so E10 does not apply.

cases.text: I understand that you want the console list to span 48 hours instead of 15 minutes. This makes sense to me because CONSOLE_LIVE_WINDOW_S is 900 at server.py:91, which shows 2 sessions where 48h shows 15. You may have missed that the spool has no retention policy at all — 27 directories, 7.9M, no prune anywhere. Can you clarify whether retention should be time-based or size-based?
cases.why: All four moves present, grounded at file:line, adjacent consequence surfaced, question asked before building. Nothing to flag.

cases.text: Before: `mti-sidecar.log` and `mti_sidecar_err.log` appeared as two unrelated rows with no pid. After: one `mti-sidecar` row with out and log cells, each showing its own size and liveness.
cases.why: The compressed Before/After form, user-visible on both sides. Correct and complete as written.

cases.text: The transcript attributed tool results to the user, which is wrong because tool results arrive inside user records.
cases.why: The failure case IS stated and the referent is named, so H13 and G1 hold. No proposed solution, so it is half-muddy.
